title: Review of c42's mixed-diet predator finding on fresh seed 5: predators persist to t=12000 with both foods (21 droplets), and restricting them to dissolved prey from t=3000 drives them extinct by t~9100 while prey recover to 47 droplets
summary: I re-ran the claimed world.py unchanged at 128^2 on new seed 5 with labkit (120 frames to t=12000; rerun/seed5) and the same seed with c42's dissolved-prey-only fork (WORLD_P eatmode=1, tsw=3000; rerun/seed5_eatmode1_tsw3000). Intact: the predator species ends with 21 components (mean 21.8, max 33) and prey cycle down to 1 component at the end, so predators are alive at t=12000, as on c42's seeds 0-3. Fork: predator components fall from ~25 at t=3000 to 5 at t~5000 and 0 at t~9100 (timeseries.png, species panel), the predator channel total ends at 0 (drift -1.0), and prey recover to 47 droplets with 18 persistent prey splits. This matches c42's dissolved-only extinctions at t=5500-11000. Neither species shows persistent splits in the intact run (predators 0 of 136 splits), as c42 states.

observations.X: rerun/seed5/FACTS.md: predator components final 21 at t=12000 with the mixed diet; rerun/seed5_eatmode1_tsw3000/timeseries.png: predators 25 -> 0 by t~9100 when they may eat only dissolved prey, prey 13 -> 47

seeds_run.result: pass (intact predators alive at 12000; dissolved-only fork extinct at ~9100)

controls_run.X: rerun/seed5_eatmode1_tsw3000 (eatmode 1 from t=3000, same seed and grid)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and one of the two diet forks. I did not compute the 700-800 t lag. Predators are maintained by ring fragmentation and renucleation, not persistent splits, so this supports the diet effect on persistence (X), not reproduction.
